rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and reveal the overall elution window and any critical pairs. The wide phi range and moderate gradient time maximize information while reducing the risk of truncation on the first run.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the next gain is reducing t_last below 10 min. Raising temperature and shortening/narrowing the gradient should compress the run while likely preserving adequate resolution, since the current minimum R has comfortable margin.

The critical pair (6,7) collapsed when the gradient was made steeper, so keep the same phi window and temperature but lengthen tG to restore slope-dependent resolution while staying near the improved sub-10 min endpoint. This isolates whether added gradient time alone can recover full resolution without giving back too much speed.

The same pair remains critical at 50 C even when the gradient is lengthened, so temperature/window likely changed selectivity unfavorably more than slope helps. Try the faster run at 50 C but restore the wider phi window from injection 1, which previously gave full resolution, to see if that recovers pair (6,7) while keeping t_last near 10 min.

The only unresolved pair worsened at 50 C, while 40 C previously gave full resolution, so test an intermediate temperature while keeping the fast successful timing/window from injection 4. This directly probes whether selectivity for pair (6,7) can be restored enough to reach R >= 1.5 without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak.

The critical pair is highly temperature-sensitive and was fully resolved at 40 C in the broader, slower scout, so test the same fast 12 min wide-window gradient at 40 C. If pair (6,7) stays resolved, this could improve on injection 1 by preserving full resolution while bringing t_last much closer to or below 10 min.

At 40 C the critical pair is much better than at 45–50 C, but still under-resolved at tG 12, so make the gradient shallower while keeping the same window and temperature. This directly tests whether modestly increasing tG can push pair (6,7) to baseline resolution while likely keeping t_last within 10 min or close to it.

Injection 7 achieved full resolution with only a small time penalty, so the next step is to shorten tG one notch to try to bring t_last to 10 min or less while staying above R = 1.5 for the critical pair. This is the direct bracket between the under-resolved 12 min run and the fully resolved 16 min run.

The best run is close to ideal but still loses score only from pair (6,7), so try a slightly narrower upper phi while keeping the same slope region and temperature. Trimming phi1 may shift selectivity around the critical mid-gradient pair without risking a time penalty, since the last peak already elutes well before 10 min.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This may push pair (6,7) to full credit, and the current t_last margin is small but still enough to test a slightly narrower window.

The best current method is just short of full resolution, while narrowing to phi1 0.85 achieved full resolution but slightly exceeded 10 min. Increasing tG at phi1 0.90 should further improve the critical pair's resolution; if t_last stays at or just under 10 min, this could reach the maximum CRF.

We now know phi1 = 0.85 gives full resolution at 14 min but just misses the 10 min target, so the key question is whether a 12 min gradient can pull t_last back under 10 min while keeping the critical pair near or above R = 1.5. This is the most direct test of whether the optimum lies at the same selective window but a slightly steeper gradient.

The best method is very close, and the critical pair is clearly temperature-sensitive, with worse behavior from 40 to 45 C. Dropping to 35 C at the current best phi window and tG may improve selectivity enough to push pair (6,7) to full resolution while likely keeping t_last near or under 10 min.

Temperature has a strong nonmonotonic effect on selectivity, and 35 C shifted the critical region enough to create a different close pair, so one more step lower is worth testing. At the current near-optimal window and tG, 30 C could separate the problematic cluster differently and potentially achieve full resolution while keeping t_last close to 10 min.

The remaining shortfall is only one mid-cluster pair at the current best conditions, so shift the whole gradient window slightly later by raising phi0 while keeping phi1, tG, and T fixed. This changes the effective phi experienced by the early-middle peaks more than the late peak and may improve selectivity in the crowded region without sacrificing the sub-10 min last peak.

Raising phi0 to 0.10 gave the best result so far and brought the critical pair very close to full credit, so now combine that improvement with the lower phi1 that previously increased resolution of pair (6,7). This should strengthen selectivity in the crowded middle while the current t_last margin leaves room for a modest increase in retention.

We have reached CRF 1.000, so only equally optimal methods are possible; now probe whether the run can be shortened while preserving full resolution. Reducing tG by one step at the same selective window and temperature is the cleanest way to test for a faster tie to the optimum.

Since shortening tG lost resolution, keep the optimal gradient shape and test whether a small temperature increase can pull t_last just below 10.00 min while retaining enough selectivity for the critical pair. This is a targeted attempt to find another 1.000 method with slightly more timing margin.

The optimum is already found, but with budget left it is worth probing whether raising phi0 one more step can retain full resolution while shaving a little more time from the front and possibly the endpoint. This keeps the successful selective window top and slope while testing a small systematic shift of the gradient band.

Injection 19 improved the timing margin while keeping full resolution, so continue one more step upward in phi0 to see whether the optimum can be maintained with even shorter retention. This is a low-risk boundary test of how far the starting composition can be raised before early peaks or the critical pair begin to compress.

Phi0 = 0.15 and phi1 = 0.85 gave a robust 1.000 score, so test one more slight narrowing of the upper window to see if full resolution can be preserved with a bit more retention compression in the useful range. This explores whether the optimum plateau extends to a still tighter gradient band.

We already have 1.000 methods, so use remaining runs to search for a faster alternative by offsetting the resolution loss from a shorter gradient with a cooler temperature that may improve selectivity. This combination targets a sub-10 min last peak while probing whether 35 C can stabilize the critical cluster under steeper conditions.

We have two 1.000 methods centered at phi1 = 0.85, so with only a few runs left, test the adjacent higher phi1 at the better phi0 = 0.15 to map the other side of the optimum plateau. This checks whether full resolution survives with a slightly wider upper window while maintaining sub-10 min elution.

With two injections left and the optimum already secured, test whether slightly higher temperature can be compensated by a shallower gradient to preserve full resolution while potentially offering a different robust 1.000 operating point. This probes the temperature–slope tradeoff around the best window without risking truncation.

For the last shot, test whether the tighter upper window that gave full resolution at 14 min can be run faster at the same favorable temperature. This is the most informative remaining boundary test around the best region, probing for a shorter fully resolved method even though 1.000 has already been achieved.
